headline: A US-funded team will measure 50,000 proteins in yeast cells to teach AI to predict when proteins start clumping in brain diseases.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a large, newly announced funded project, but only the first data-building phase is funded now.
importance_line: It aims at earlier warning of brain diseases such as Alzheimer's and ALS, but the first two years only build data and models, and any treatment benefit is not yet shown.
summary: The Stowers Institute for Medical Research says it is part of NATIVE-ID, a project led by the University of California, Berkeley's Innovative Genomics Institute and funded with up to $28.6 million by ARPA-H, the US government's advanced health research agency, to train AI to predict when proteins linked to Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS and Huntington's are likely to clump and damage cells. Stowers' lab will receive about $4.1 million over two years to measure how 50,000 proteins clump in yeast cells, producing more than 10 billion measurements as training data, because AI still struggles with the roughly one-third of proteins that have no stable shape; this first phase only builds datasets and models, with testing of possible therapeutics planned for a second phase.
notes: Institution's own announcement; no independent view in the release.
